solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Book into capital place for convalescing?

indicators.note: the book's abbreviation is put into the capital city's name

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy
Esth is the standard abbreviation for the Old Testament book of Esther

explanation.surface: A traveller checks into a city hotel to recover from illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' looks like a verb meaning reserve, but it is a book of the Bible, abbreviated. The question mark flags a definition by description.
explanation.definitionFit: A rest home is a residence where people recuperate or are looked after, so it is literally a place to convalesce.

clue.text: Healthy old boy going into decline

indicators.note: the former pupil is put inside the word for decline

parts.note: to rust is to decay, decline
OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: A healthy elderly man is starting to go downhill.
explanation.definitionFit: Robust means strong and in good health, a synonym for healthy.

clue.text: Commander half-revealed weapon

indicators.note: half signals that only the opening part of a word for revealed is used

parts.note: shown means revealed
a gun is a weapon

explanation.surface: A military leader partly displays his arms.
explanation.definitionFit: A shogun was a hereditary military ruler in feudal Japan, effectively its commander-in-chief.

clue.text: Fellow lifted blade outside for one's roadside bushes

parts.note: he is a fellow, a male person

indicators.note: lifted in a down answer means read upwards, so backwards
the blade goes round the abbreviation for example

parts.note: a sword is a blade
eg, for example, means for one

explanation.surface: A man raises his sword, perhaps against wayside shrubbery.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'lifted' means read upwards, so the whole blade-round-example unit turns over, giving DGEROWS.
explanation.definitionFit: Hedgerows are lines of shrubs and small trees bordering country lanes and fields.

clue.text: Curmudgeonly, the writer and a hooligan imbibing alcohol

parts.note: the writer refers to the setter, me

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so the alcohol goes inside

parts.note: ned is Scottish slang for a young hooligan
spirit is strong alcohol

explanation.surface: A grumpy writer and a thug are both drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: NED is Scottish slang for a young thug, roughly a British 'chav'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mean-spirited means ungenerous and grudging, close to the sour temper of a curmudgeon.

clue.text: Dance that's trendy and hard work

parts.note: hip means fashionable, trendy
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: A fashionable dance style that is also exhausting to perform.
explanation.definitionFit: Hip-hop is a style of street dance performed to rap music.

clue.text: Lying motionless in bed, having removed clothing

indicators.note: stripping off the clothing means losing the outer letters of the word

parts.note: a berth is a bed on a ship or train

explanation.surface: Someone lies still in bed after undressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bed' looks like the place you lie, but it supplies a sleeping-car word whose outer letters are stripped, leaving ERT.
explanation.definitionFit: Inert means without power to move, still and inactive.

clue.text: Sound dissatisfied? Cheer up as policeman comes in

indicators.note: the policeman enters the reversed cheer
up in a down answer means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: hurrah is a cheer
MP is a military policeman

explanation.surface: A grumble from the crowd as the officer enters, ending the cheers.
explanation.definitionFit: Harrumph is to clear the throat or snort to show disapproval, a grumpy noise of discontent.

clue.text: Some wandered briefly in garden

parts.note: part means some

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, dropping the final letter

parts.note: to err is originally to wander, so erred means wandered

explanation.surface: Some people strolled for a short while in a garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A parterre is a formal garden of ornamental beds laid out in a pattern.

clue.text: Award boy collected in New York's theatreland

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are gathered up and put together in a new order

explanation.surface: A young actor wins a prize in the heart of the New York stage world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' seems a natural anagram signal, but it belongs to the definition; 'collected' does the rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadway is the Manhattan avenue whose theatres form New York's main commercial stage district.

clue.text: Youngster causing havoc finally shot by mistake

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word shot

parts.note: an error is a mistake

explanation.surface: A troublesome child is finally shot dead by accident.
explanation.definitionFit: A little terror is an idiom for an unruly, mischievous child.

clue.text: A mostly very nice time producing realistic movies

indicators.note: producing suggests making something new from the material, here the letters
mostly means almost all, dropping the last letter of very

explanation.surface: A pleasant evening out at the pictures, almost.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinema vérité is a documentary film style aiming at naturalistic realism.

clue.text: Fry odd parts of sea turtle

indicators.note: the first, third, fifth and further odd-numbered letters of the two words are taken

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction: fry up some bits of sea turtle.
explanation.definitionFit: To sauté is to fry quickly in a little hot fat, so it is a kind of frying.

clue.text: Good man who wrote fantastic tales in UK

indicators.note: fantastic suggests something wild and unreal, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A worthy author penned fanciful stories set in Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good man' stands for a saint (ST); this one was the author of the third Gospel and Acts.
explanation.definitionFit: Luke the Evangelist, a saint, is traditionally credited with writing a Gospel and the Acts of the Apostles.

clue.text: Someone has to kill serial criminal in sensational novel

parts.note: bod is informal British for a person, someone
to ice someone is slang for to kill them
a ripper is a serial killer, as in Jack the Ripper

explanation.surface: A thriller plot in which someone must murder a serial killer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodice-ripper is a lurid historical romance novel full of passion and seduction.

clue.text: Irish officer initially scorns forged medal

indicators.note: initially picks out the first letter of officer
forged means made, faked, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: An Irish officer looks down on a counterfeit decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iron Cross is a German military decoration for bravery.

clue.text: Least courageous warriors in Europe and America?

indicators.note: the warriors are placed within the region

parts.note: the West means Europe and North America together
an impi is a body of Zulu warriors

explanation.surface: Wondering whether Western soldiers are the most cowardly.
explanation.walkthrough: An IMPI is a Zulu regiment; the question mark marks Europe and America as an example of 'the West'.
explanation.definitionFit: A wimp is a feeble, timid person, so the wimpiest is the most lacking in courage.

clue.text: Keeps an eye on eggs — clutch, you say?

indicators.note: you say tells us the pieces are spoken, sounding like the answer

parts.note: ova are eggs and to clutch is to seize, so said together these give 'ova seize'

explanation.surface: A broody bird watches over its clutch of eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clutch' wants to be a clutch of eggs, but it is the verb, grab.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversee is to supervise, watching over something.

clue.text: Detective wearing very little confronting dangerous creature on island

indicators.note: confronting means facing up to, so the next piece sits right beside the first
in an across answer, the creature placed on the island comes after it

parts.note: someone in just a vest is wearing very little
a gator, short for alligator, is a dangerous reptile

explanation.surface: A scantily clad sleuth faces a dangerous animal on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: An investigator is someone who looks into crimes, a synonym for a detective.

clue.text: John is able to dance

parts.note: john and can are both American slang for a toilet
can means is able to

explanation.surface: A man called John knows how to dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John' looks like a name, but it is slang for a lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: The cancan is a high-kicking dance from Parisian music halls.

clue.text: One teaching correct pronunciation about to swallow energy drink

indicators.note: the reversed pair takes the energy letter inside it
about means turned round, so the two pieces are read backwards

parts.note: a don is a university teacher
RP, Received Pronunciation, is the standard accent of British English
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An elocution teacher is about to down an energy drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Received Pronunciation is the prestige British accent; 'about' turns teacher and accent round to PRNOD before the energy goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Pernod is a French aniseed-flavoured aperitif, a branded drink.

clue.text: Go on about trailing first lady's representative around

indicators.note: trailing means following behind, so this piece comes last
around means turned round, so the two pieces before it are read backwards

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in Genesis, so first lady's is EVE'S
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Keep talking about a president's wife's agent who follows her everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first lady' suggests a president's wife, but here she is Eve; 'around' turns her and the agent over, giving PERSEVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To go on with something despite difficulty is to persist, which is the sense here.

clue.text: Music in sci-fi film due for redistribution

parts.note: E.T. is Spielberg's science-fiction film

indicators.note: redistribution means sharing out again in a new pattern, so the letters move

explanation.surface: A soundtrack in an alien movie needs reworking.
explanation.definitionFit: An étude is a short musical study written to practise a technique.

clue.text: Long-necked bird beginning to eat lots of herrings at first

indicators.note: the herrings come first, before the opening letter

parts.note: a cran is a measure of fresh herrings, about 750 fish

indicators.note: beginning to points to the first letter of the word eat

explanation.surface: A wading bird starts tucking into a big haul of herrings.
explanation.walkthrough: A cran is an old Scottish measure of fresh herrings, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Cranes are tall wading birds noted for their long necks and legs.

clue.text: All one can see of much-visited tower, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the tower's name is to be heard, not read

parts.note: the Eiffel Tower in Paris draws millions of visitors

explanation.surface: Visitors to the famous Paris landmark get a full view.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyeful is as much as the eye can take in, a full view of something.

clue.text: Spanish bar includes whale on menu's starter

indicators.note: in an across answer, the bar with the whale is placed after the starting letter
the starter of the menu is its opening letter, not a first course
the pub's name holds the whale inside it

parts.note: an inn is a pub, a bar
the orca is the killer whale

explanation.surface: A Spanish tapas bar features whale as the first item on its menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'menu's starter' hints at a first course, but means just the letter M.
explanation.definitionFit: A Minorcan is a native of Minorca, one of Spain's Balearic Islands, so the word is a kind of Spanish.

clue.text: Ciabatta's terrific: consumer's tucked into that

definitions.note: read as consumer is, the definition being a consumer who samples food

indicators.note: the letters are tucked away inside the run of words

explanation.surface: A diner praises the bread after tucking into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucked into' suggests eating but signals that the letters lie inside 'Ciabatta's terrific'; 'that' points back to those words.
explanation.definitionFit: A taster samples food or drink, so is someone who consumes a little of it.

clue.text: Methodical when working in long grass

indicators.note: in places the two short words within the grass

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass growing by water
as can mean when, as in 'as he left'
on means working, functioning

explanation.surface: Someone methodical while out working in the tall grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Reasoned means logically thought out, so systematic or methodical.
